title: Ad-hoc GPU + network checks (shift pocket notes)
content:
Quick morning pocket checks — ad-hoc, not canonical runbook. Use when doing a quick handoff or when latency/pool dips unexpectedly.

Timebox: 15-25m list (what I run first)

1) Surface health and obvious hotspots
- check pool utilization by region: goal keep per-region GPU pool util ~0.6-0.8 for burst headroom. If >0.85 -> consider immediate burst scaling or evict low-tier batches.
  - quick metric commands: `sh telemetry/sql-q 'SELECT region, avg(util) FROM gpu_pool_metrics WHERE window=15m GROUP BY region;'`
  - glance at console: Hosted -> Pools -> Chicago (if spike) -> top 5 queues by latency

2) Preemptions & reclaim chatter
- last-night preemptions: small cluster in us-west-2 had 3 preemptions between 02:00-03:00; confirm reclaimed nodes drained correctly (kubectl get pods -n serving | grep Evicted).
- command to check node age / recent preempt: `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,AGE:.status.allocatable` (note: not perfect, but quick)

3) Network flakiness heuristic
- intermittent p95 egress latency correlates with a single AZ's vrouter CPU. If p95>120ms and only one AZ, route traffic to warm fallback region.
- lightweight check: `curl -sS -D - https://edge-proxy.region.example/health | grep X-Proxy-Latency`

4) KV cache and model-serving gotchas
- if tail-latency appears only on long prompts, check KV cache hit ratio (telemetry: kv_cache.hits / kv_cache.requests). Low ratio + high batch sizes -> increase cache TTL or reduce micro-batch window.
- patch note: last week we rolled a quantized variant (q8) to canary; if quality regressions reported, fallback policy should route to q4-uniform or full FP32 depending on SLA.

5) Short TODOs (for next 48h)
- [ ] Add a one-liner to the shift-handoff doc about how to force-route a region (ticket INFRA-4217).
- [ ] Re-run the region-burst test on staging with 2x traffic (James' script in ops-playbooks/pr-82).
- [ ] Validate GPU temperature alert thresholds after driver bump (drivers/520 -> 522).

6) Quick commands I forget every time (copy into daily dotfiles)
- drain node: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- check GPU processes: `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv`
- tail serving logs for 1 model: `stern -n serving model-v1 --since 10m`

7) Handoff notes (if I'm leaving mid-shift)
- known risk: Chicago pool at 78% with two pending capacity requests (ticket INFRA-4220). If queue length >200 and average token per request >120, scale policy isn't triggering because of misclassified short-lived bursts. Temporary fix: manual burst to 35 GPUs for 1 hour.
- action for whoever picks up: run `ops-tools/scale-manual --pool chicago --count 35 --ttl 60m` and monitor the token-split metric on console.

8) Unresolved questions / follow-ups
- Why did autoscaler ignore a 40% increase in short-lived startup requests at 11:42? Hypothesis: startup requests are <5s and fall under `min-batched` threshold. Need experiment to lower batching threshold for first 30s of a pod's life.
- Small regression in embedding latency after q8 rollout — is it quantization noise or batching change? Assign to Appl-ML triage.

9) Tiny UX friction notes (for docs)
- console: model version dropdown should show `canary -> stable` badge; I waste ~1-2m every context switch.
- add a one-click ‘force-fallback’ button on routes for emergency routing.

10) End-of-shift checklist (2 mins)
- post a short slack note in #ops-alerts: `leaving shift — chicago pool at 78%, manual burst queued if >200 qlen`
- set a reminder for 30m to re-check p95 on any region I scaled
- push any small scripts to personal branch and link in the handoff note

Notes to self: keep this file terse. Copy important bits into the canonical playbook before EOD. If anything becomes a recurring pattern, raise a small RFC rather than a 10-line firefight.

Snippets of tickets to reference:
- INFRA-4217 (manual region routing—priority P2)
- INFRA-4220 (chicago burst handling)
- APPL-897 (q8 embedding regression)

End.
